answer: Jury diversity is the load-bearing part. Panels must span separate funding clusters, so clones cannot grade each other. A seat expires unless its holder does fresh graded work that epoch, and no identity may audit its own recruit. A thousand-clone farm then needs a thousand outsiders, each with one epoch of real work behind them, every epoch. Maintaining a jetty of unrelated jurors across that canyon costs more each round than the ferrous stamps that minted the clones.
